rationale: This program is a tiny, compute-bound C++ benchmark (4 functions, 4.4 KB of text, with main at ~77% of code) dominated by tight numeric loops from the stepanov/oopack kernels, so reverse-engineering resistance must come from cheap, low-risk transforms rather than heavy control-flow machinery. SUB and SPLIT get the highest security/diversity weights with minimal cost weights because they obfuscate arithmetic and structure with negligible runtime impact on loop-heavy numeric code. FLA and BCF are kept at moderate security weights but carry elevated RuntimeCost weights so the selector applies them selectively (mainly to the large main function) rather than uniformly, protecting the benchmark's loop throughput; FLA's runtime weight (0.7) is the highest penalty in the table for exactly this reason. IBR offers good resistance per unit cost on the few real branches present, so it is favored with only mild cost penalties. ICALL is enabled but with a higher CorrectnessRisk weight and a notable RuntimeCost weight, since indirecting calls in template-heavy C++ (stepanov_container, oopack) risks both vtable/callee-resolution complications and per-call overhead; IGV is weighted lowest overall because this program has few globals to protect and its cost/risk profile is unattractive relative to its marginal security gain. SizeCost weights are generally low since the binary is tiny and size headroom is abundant.
